chunk_map.heading: Pick one threat, record the decision (H1/lede)
Phase 1: Run the threat scan across your mapped surface
Read the threat list, expect more than you'll use
Phase 2: Pick the one threat worth hardening against
Push back on the incident story, land the mitigation
Phase 3: Write the decision as an ADR
Read the ADR, check the voice and the lens
Ask whether the ADR loads into future sessions
Save the map and the STRIDE walk before you clear

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Referent resolution under a sequential deck read.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Harm: a slide leaning on a referent never named strands the reader mid-deck. Traced every candidate: chunk 0 line 5 'the main quest window (*m3-security*)' and line 7 'the map you built' are pre-established by this module's earlier includes (verified in earn-the-trust.md Start here order: open-the-side-quest.md line 17 names Session (new,"m3-security") and line 5 'Security is the main quest'; map-the-access-surface.md lines 5/26/52/58 reinforce m3-security repeatedly — both files precede this one in the module's include order). Chunk 1 line 22 'the access-surface map from Exercise 1' resolves via the unpacked claim itself ('access-surface map' is unambiguous, session-artifact carve-out). Chunk 6 lines 63-64 'The Decision section'/'the Alternatives considered section' resolve against chunk 5's fenced prompt (raw line 58 lists 'Context / Decision / Consequences / Alternatives considered'), which renders visibly on the slide even though fenced content is exempt from being scored for violations itself. Chunk 7 line 68 'the M3 worktree'/'the side-quest' resolves both within its own chunk (line 69 unpacks it) and against this module's own signposting (earn-the-trust.md line 22 'Fork a sibling git worktree'; open-the-side-quest.md lines 5/13/37 establish 'side-quest lane' fully, preceding this file). No never-named or vague-with-full-history referent found in any chunk.

Harm: pointing at another file by position only works if the deck starts where the writer assumed. Chunk 1 line 22 names the source by claim ('the access-surface map') in the same breath it says 'from Exercise 1' — the claim alone is sufficient to resolve the referent (only one access-surface map exists in the training), so this passes the rule's own worked example shape ('unpacked in the same sentence'). No sentence points at a prior file solely by position ('the opening lecture said...') without also naming its claim.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Every backward reference points at a beat that exists.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Harm: a stranded callback sends the student hunting for a beat that was cut. Verified against earn-the-trust.md's current Start here list (read directly, not from cache): '[Exercise: Open the side quest]' (line 33) and '[Exercise: Map the access surface]' (line 37) both exist and precede this file (line 39) in the current include order. Both backward references in this file ('the map you built' / 'the access-surface map from Exercise 1' -> Map the access surface; 'the side-quest' / 'the M3 worktree' -> Open the side quest) resolve to beats confirmed present in the live module file.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Live-demo beats survive a text read.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Harm: a guess/predict beat whose answer is narrated above it teaches nothing. Only ask-then-reveal shape in the file is chunk 8: the ask (line 74, 'Ask Claude whether this ADR rides into future sessions automatically') precedes the reveal (line 78, "Claude's answer: no...") in reading order, both same chunk and correctly sequenced. No other guess/predict beat exists in the file.

Harm: a slide that says nothing standalone. Checked the shortest chunks specifically: chunk 2 (2 bullets, no fence) carries its own claim about why the scan over-produces and how to gauge scan depth; chunk 4 (2 bullets, no fence) carries the push-back rationale plus the land-the-mitigation instruction; chunk 6 (2 bullets) carries the voice-check plus the STRIDE-as-tool-not-lens worked example. None is a bare wait-state or single context-dependent fragment.

Harm: a header the chunk's own content contradicts misleads a skimming reader. Checked all 9 '##' headers against their bodies line by line: each states exactly what its chunk does (e.g. 'Check where the ADR landed' -> body checks main-repo-vs-worktree path; 'Ask whether the ADR loads into future sessions' -> body asks then answers that exact question). No contradiction found in any chunk.

Harm: cadence tics read as machine-authored on a slide. Checked all five sub-items across the full body independently: (a) 'Not X. Not Y. Z.' triple -- none ('One threat, not five' at line 36 is a single two-part contrast, not the banned three-part shape). (b) anaphora/epistrophe triples -- none. (c) self-grading superlatives -- none (grepped for 'most useful'/'one of the' style phrasing, zero hits in body). (d) number+own-retraction -- none (the four time budgets at lines 3, 17, 34, 51 are plain durations, no hedge attached). (e) abstraction-noun stacks -- none; vocabulary stays concrete throughout (access surface, incident story, ADR, worktree). (f) verb triplets with an empty leg -- none. Aggregated into this one rule-7 entry per the completeness contract.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Internal dialect never lands on a slide.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Harm: repo/authorial vocabulary a room can't parse. Grepped body for 'compendium', 'firing', 'forcing function', 'beat', 'mood', 'Connections' (as proper noun) -- zero hits in body (all appear only in the maintainer/backing blocks, which are cut). 'Access surface' / 'the mapped surface' (chunk 0, chunk 1 header) is domain-standard security vocabulary (cf. 'attack surface'), covered by the rule's own carve-out distinguishing this from authorial 'surface'-as-writing-jargon. 'main quest'/'side quest'/'worktree' are the training's own established teaching vocabulary (earned in the prior exercise, not leaked internal dialect).

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Emphasis budget -- bold is for handles, and go very lightly.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Harm: over-bolding trains readers to ignore bold as a signal. Every bold span in the body is widget/label chrome the file's own maintainer note (raw line 97) already accept-notes: chunk 0's **Time:**/**Window:**/**What you do:**/**What you build:**/**The point:**, chunk 9's **Worth keeping?**/**What happened:**/**What this sets up:**. Scanned every bullet lead across all 9 chunks for a bolded whole-sentence lead (the pre-2026-07-09 monoculture shape) -- none found.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Presence precedes content -- verify against the composed deck, not long-read.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Harm: content invisible in the deck gets rules 1-9 applied to a slide that never renders. This file is included in earn-the-trust.md via the standard '[Exercise: Threat-model with STRIDE](exercises/threat-model-with-stride.md)' link (verified live at line 39), the same include shape every AE101 exercise uses to reach the composed deck via .phase--exercise / section.module wrapping. No phase-less bare prose section exists in this file. Ran the mechanical checks below (rules 11/12/14) directly against this file path and all three executed and reported per-file results, corroborating the file is a recognized slide-bearing unit.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Heading grammar is the mood switch, and it is load-bearing.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Harm: a declarative heading inside an exercise where none is earned muddies the imperative/phase-label mood exercises need. Checked all 9 '##' headings verbatim: 3 are 'Phase N: <label>' phase labels, 6 are imperative verb phrases ('Read the threat list...', 'Push back on...', 'Read the ADR...', 'Check where...', 'Ask whether...', 'Save the map...'). None is a bare declarative claim; consistent exercise mood throughout.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: A bullet earns its slot or dies -- three classes that read as rigour and carry nothing.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Harm: a doctrine restatement / self-referential design note / aphorism kicker adds no move, object, tell, or priority the slide doesn't already carry. Checked each of the three classes against the CURRENT body (this rule and this file's 2026-08-25 lean pass share a date; the diff against 1abb84c6 shows the maintainer already cut six near-miss instances -- 'It will have more entries than you want to deal with.', 'You are picking a single threat worth hardening against.', 'You save it as the ADR next.', the Phase-3 compliance-checkbox duplicate, half the worktree-inference bullet, 'Not everything survived to disk.', and the closer's CISO line). Closest surviving candidates, each checked and kept: chunk 2 line 29 'The output over-produces on purpose... that rejection is the point' restates the lede's 'STRIDE's value is rejection, not enumeration' but instantiates it at the exact moment the student feels the long list, which is new work (explains WHY, not a re-announcement); chunk 8 line 79 'that explicit list is the lesson' foreshadows M4's payoff rather than narrating this file's own pedagogy; chunk 6 line 64 'You decide.' is a permission-grant, not a koan restating the header. No surviving instance of doctrine restatement, self-referential design commentary, or aphorism kicker found.
